analysis_type: High-precision analytic critical-radius and fixed-grid sensitivity audit for native Chwirut1 exponential denominator certificates and conservative prediction envelopes; no refitting, radius optimization or probability-region claim

critical_radius_rule.unit_support: For each endpoint x, compute s(x)=sqrt(C_b2b2+2*C_b2b3*x+C_b3b3*x^2) using the frozen covariance matrix
critical_radius_rule.endpoint_radius: When d_hat(x)>0, rho(x)=d_hat(x)/s(x); when d_hat(x)<=0, no positive denominator-safe radius exists at that endpoint
critical_radius_rule.fold_radius: rho_fold=min(rho_left,rho_right); record the limiting endpoint and both endpoint values
critical_radius_rule.strict_rule: Positive denominator certification requires radius < rho_fold; radius = rho_fold gives d_min = 0 and is not strictly positive, so no finite prediction envelope is generated
critical_radius_rule.geometric_scope: The critical radius is a geometric property of the selected ellipsoid and continuous interval, not a confidence level, optimal radius, physical parameter estimate or universal maximum
critical_radius_rule.negative_control: For every fold, verify that half the analytic critical radius is accepted and the exact critical radius is rejected by the same outward-rounded denominator implementation

grid_rule.selection: All five radii are frozen before inspecting case outcomes and are reported without selecting a preferred or optimal radius
grid_rule.case_evaluation: For each fold and radius, evaluate the continuous denominator at both endpoints and record certified or unavailable status, limiting reason and analytic radius relation
grid_rule.envelope_evaluation: Only certified cases generate original nonlinear prediction envelopes at the fold's unique held-out distances and residual upper bounds for all observations
grid_rule.width_audit: Report maximum and median envelope widths and residual upper bounds per case; unavailable cases retain null bounds rather than fabricated values
grid_rule.center_consistency: Require every available center prediction to remain inside its envelope and actual residual not to exceed its upper bound; this is arithmetic consistency, not probability coverage or external validation
grid_rule.grid_maximum: Report the largest certified radius within the fixed grid separately from the analytic critical radius; never call the grid maximum the exact safe maximum

baseline_rule.preservation: Recompute the radius-4 case and require certified_fold_count=5, available_point_count=214, covered_point_count=214, violation_point_count=0, unavailable_point_count=0 and center_prediction_envelope_mismatch_count=0, matching the frozen baseline totals
baseline_rule.historical_preservation: Do not rewrite the baseline bounds file or its report

numerical_rule.engine: Reuse the frozen 80-digit mpmath support, denominator and original nonlinear envelope implementation
numerical_rule.outward_rounding: Retain the 1e-24 relative margin and nextafter outward conversion
numerical_rule.certificate_class: High-precision numerical interval certificate, not exact rational algebra
numerical_rule.failure_preservation: Non-positive centers, non-positive-definite matrices, exact critical radii and unavailable cases are retained explicitly

output_rule.word: papers/前沿共生Chwirut1原生椭球半径敏感性_图文完整版.docx

prohibitions: No refitting, changed centers, changed covariance matrices, changed folds or post-hoc radius selection
No acceptance of the exact critical radius as strictly denominator-positive
No finite prediction or residual bound for unavailable or exact-critical cases
No probability, confidence, posterior, calibrated-coverage, optimal-radius or physical-endogeneity claim
No use of center-prediction containment or actual-residual coverage as independent scientific validation
No calling the largest certified grid radius the exact or universal safe maximum
No exact rational-certificate claim for the high-precision numerical intervals
No description of Chwirut1 as independent of the Chwirut2 study or native model family
No hiding of unavailable cases, limiting endpoints, wide envelopes or numerical failures
